utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber was expecting a witness, but we're to have a motion instead. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, we have had an opportunity to discuss the issue of documents with the Prosecution in the course of last night and this morning and I'm grateful my colleague provided with us information which hopefully will simplify Your Honour's decision. There are five documents which we would seek to tender and two which we would ask the Chamber to MFI and I will start with those documents in relation to which there is no observation on the part of the Prosecution. The first such document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D1098. Your Honour will recall that this is an Official Note taken by the UBK, the state security services. It's dated 8th of 2002 [sic]. And Mr. Kuehnel indicated that he believed it was one of the document which he personally obtained from those records. The part of the document which was put to Mr. Kuehnel concerned one of the alleged victim Mr. Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The date appears incompletely in the transcript. It was the 8th of?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Of May, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D273, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second document is Rule 65 ter 1D1138.1. This is a list of members of the security of the president. Those -- it contains the names of members of the presidential security and they have been put to the witness in relation to phone records which have been tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor. We believe that the names that are relevant to Your Honour's consideration have been read to the witness and he has adopted the information which was of relevance to this matter. We believe however that the list itself may be of assistance to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D274, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D1141. This is a decision signed by the then minister of the interior of the 8th of November of 1991 [sic] concerning the appointment of persons responsible to initiate disciplinary proceedings. Your Honour will recall this was the first of two decisions concerning this matter and the date of that document is 8th November 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Correct date is 1999, not 1991 as appears at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D275, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document Your Honour was the follow-up or the following decision concerning the name matter dated the 20th of September of 2005 and also signed by the then minister of the interior Mr. Mihajlovski. It's 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D276, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The only document which gives rise to an objection at this stage is Rule 65 ter 995. This is a document that actually appeared on the Prosecution Rule 65 ter list. This is the scheme prepared by Dr. Jakovski of the hands of Mr. Qaili, the deceased, which indicates that Mr. Qaili tested positive to nitrate particles and it's essentially a copy of both hands with the markings of the positions of the nitrate particles. Your Honour will recall that the content of the document was put to Mr. Kuehnel in cross-examination. Mr. Kuehnel obtained that very document from Mr. -- from Dr. Jakovski himself. I will also indicate for the record that this very document, Rule 65 ter 995, was used by the Prosecution in its examination-in-chief of Dr. Eichner on the 3rd of September of this year at page 4455 to 4459. The issue of the test and finding made by Dr. Jakovski on the hands of Mr. Qaili were also discussed quite extensionly with Dr. Jakovski himself, in particular, Your Honour, at page 2292, to 2293. For completeness of the record we'd also indicate that the Prosecution has already tendered a particular document which is Exhibit P49 at page 33 which is in effect the report or the short summary report written by Mr. -- Dr. Jakovski in relation to the test carried out on the hands of Mr. Qaili.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe my colleague Ms. Issa will address these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, good afternoon. The only issue I had, Your Honour, is the mere fact that the document itself was actually not shown to the witness and he was not able to comment on the document itself and it could have been shown, so I'm objecting on that basis, although it -- clearly I can see that these matters were discussed with one other witness, as my colleague points out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your concern would be met if the witness, when he returns, were to have the document put to him. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So there can be no doubt we might follow that course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Simply for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And for that purpose you have leave to reopen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honour. Simply for the record, the name of Mr. Kuehnel actually appears on the top corner of the documents, but I will certainly do so and I'm grateful. Your Honour, if we could move for a second to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could we have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now there's one brief matter that Mr. Mettraux needs to just finish up with, which we now realise hadn't been dealt with. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I have only a few more question for you. Do you recall conducting with an interview with Dr. Jakovski earlier this year, in February 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall reviewing and receiving a number of documents from Mr. Jakovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in general terms, there were documents which were attached, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please bring up Rule 65 ter 995, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you recall this document being one of the documents which you received from Dr. Jakovski in the course of your interview?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I also recognise my handwriting on the top left part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that this particular document pertained to a so-called paraffin glove test which had been conducted on the body of Mr. Qaili. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this document is dated the 14th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no. And we can also see that somebody has written over this so I think you can see 14 and 15 in the right-hand corner there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. And is it correct also, Mr. Kuehnel, that this document subsequently was attached to the statement of Dr. Jakovski which you prepared on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D279, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I have to correct myself. I said there had been something written over and it was 14 and 15. It was, I think, 11 -- it's actually very hard to decipher. I think it is 11 and 15. I can't quite read it. But 11th, wouldn't make any sense. It's got to be 14 and 15 and it must be wrong in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hello to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, we are Defence counsels of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Mr. Kuehnel, during your investigation on the case, you established that Mr. Johan Tarculovski, in 2001, was married to Valentina Radulevic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is general knowledge. I did not especially investigate and establish this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Valentina Radulevic is a famous handball player in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. She's also known beyond the borders of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, she has also played for foreign teams, in Austria, Denmark. Would you agree would me?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you established that in 2001, Johan Tarculovski and Valentina Radulevic lived together in a flat in the suburb of Irodrom [phoen] in Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say this with certainty, because I do not know whether they lived all this time together.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you check in which flat they lived in 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you check which telephone number was used?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information I received through the information obtained through -- from connection data.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Please, if the witness could be shown 536 Exhibit, page 3. This is a phone list of outgoing calls from the phone number 070279417. This page was shown to you by my learned colleague from the Prosecution. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And in row 3, you see the name Valentina Radulevic?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you said that this was a phone number owned by Valentina Radulevic?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what one concludes when one reads this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: With this you established the fact that Johan Tarculovski made a contact with Valentina Radulevic on the 10th of August, 2001, and this is how you based your opinion that Johan Tarculovski used this phone number, 070279417, on the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I explained it in these very words. What I did say was one can conclude from this that between the two phone numbers listed here and between the telephone number which we believe Johan Tarculovski has been using at that time has established a connection with the other telephone number which Valentina Radulevic is listed as being the subscriber.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see that the connection was with the phone number 02469882, as a phone number that belongs to the subscriber Valentina Radulevic?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is written here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you check whether it was a mobile phone number or a land-line phone number?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I read this, this would be a land-line. Because at that time, and this is general knowledge, all mobile telephone numbers begin with the digits 070, and at a later period 075 numbers were introduced. The 02 prefix indicates to me that this is an indeed a land-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But did you -- you did not point out this during your testimony. Would you agree with me on this?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference between the mobile telephone number 070 and 02, I did not explain in detail so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please see the same line, right side, you see the address Kuzman Jusifovski. Do you see that on the monitor? This is the address of Valentina Radulevic?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Wuld you agree with me that this is the home land-line phone number of Valentina Radulevic on street Kuzman Jusifovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here is the subscriber information which obviously has been entered into this form by the telephone provider. Whether this is the official place of residence or another address, could be a billing address, I cannot tell you which.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: By reading this, it is obvious that Kuzman Jusifovski street is an address of Valentina Radulevic. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could get this impression when one read this is document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You knew that in August 2001, Valentina Radulevic was in Austria where she played handball. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what would be the logic for Johan Tarculovski to call his wife on the home land-line phone number if he had known that his wife was in Austria? Wouldn't you agree he would call her on the mobile phone number?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible. Although I do not know on which date Mrs. Valentina Radulevic went to Austria. But it has been known for some time that Ms. Radulevic was in Austria at the time. Whether Mr. Johan Tarculovski might have called a family member, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is your assumption.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know if Valentina Radulevic and Johan Tarculovski had any kids?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the phone number, 070279417, was used by the security of late president Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This telephone number is certainly an official telephone number, which is listed officially as a service number. It is, however, our point of view that Johan Tarculovski, at the very least at the specific period of the incidents concerned, used this telephone number, and other periods of questioning I have also established this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with my conclusion that the questions that I just asked you about the third row on the phone list, that some colleague called Johan Tarculovski on his home phone number?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is speculative and I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But, as an assumption, is it possible, not as a speculation?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to that. I believe the witness has already indicated that he doesn't know and the question is speculative, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski -- Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours, I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please see the same page but four rows below. Do you see the name of Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to this listing, from the number, 070279417, there was a connection with a phone number under the name Johan Tarculovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you now agree with me that the most correct conclusion would be about who used the phone number, 070279417, would be the security of the president, Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not at all agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So Johan Tarculovski could have called Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Johan Tarculovski can certainly have called his own number. He can call his fixed-line phone under which he is registered. And as far as I'm aware, even family members are registered as living under this same address Dizonska 25, so this looks to me like an ordinary user profile, which certainly would not constitute evidence, although a very credible indication for the use of this mobile telephone as would correspond to ordinary user patterns would, if not at home, call the home telephone. This works both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you check who lived on Dizonska street in 2001.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this information is in RFA 77. And apart from that, we also received further information. I would have to check - I'm not currently entirely sure - but I think also Mr. Tarculovski's father is registered there. But I would have to check up on this again. We have several times established that in the course of the various summonses which we tried to deliver, or have delivered, that Mr. Johan Tarculovski is registered as living under this address. Although he did not actually -- he was not actually there, at least at this time in 2004 or 2005, when we attempted to summon him. Any further information concerning his address is also in RFA 75. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that Johan Tarculovski's father died in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So it couldn't have been that he lived on that address in 2001 if he died in 1999. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not entirely sure. But the fact is only registered there is also possible [as interpreted]. But I would have to check up on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You had an information from the Macedonian government that the phone number, 070279417, was used by Todorovski Gjorgi employed in the security section. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did receive this information. The last time this information had been transmitted was as part of the attachment pertaining to RFA 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have received this information as early as in September 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did receive this several times. I believe it also is part of RFA 77. Two or three times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But, at any rate, you had it as of September 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, but, again, I would have to check this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And until 2007, you did not make any attempt to establish contact with the person Gjorgi Todorovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: So far certainly we have not interviewed him. It is possible that I or my colleagues, in 2004, attempted to localise either this or another person, but I do not have a clear recollection of this, because I myself, until mid-2005, did not have direct contacts with the ministry myself. Such contacts were organised by one of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But neither you nor colleagues have requested from the Macedonian authorities, all the way until 2007, to provide you an opportunity to interview this person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is indeed correct. Certainly that could have been done earlier. (redacted) specifically those with Mario Jurisic and others --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that neither you nor a single colleague of yours has asked questions with regards to the name Gjorgi Todorovski to any of the witnesses during their interviews?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness -- actually, the witness already sees the Exhibit 5369 [as interpreted]. Could we show him page number ten, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if can I just make a correction for the transcript. In the transcript the exhibit has been referred to as 5369 or 536, and I believe the exhibit number is actually P00369. Sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you see now page 10. Do you see the rows 23 to 27, and the name Nusret Bajrami written there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the phone number, 070279417, has, on the 12th of August, 2001, had seven phone conversations. Can you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is throughout the day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like this, yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Considering the name and the family name of the person Nusret Bajrami, is it correct that that would be a person of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You might conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you or members of your team of investigators tried to establish contact with the person Nusret Bajrami to check who phoned him on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you did not feel it necessary to check the Albanian who appears in the listing, to check who has phoned him on the 12th of August, 2001, ten times?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been a possibility, yes. But they're lots of other contacts contained in this list that we didn't contact either so far. As far as I know, there must be about almost 2.000 contacts. Of course, it's 12th of August, yes, but that was not a priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that all persons you see in front of you on this page were contacted, all of them apart from Nusret Bajrami. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But as far as Mr. Najdovski is concerned, I'm not sure. Vlado Janev, yes; Dejan Jovkov, yes; and Aco Mladenov, yes. Not sure about Aco Mladenov, no, I mixed him up with somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer. And when I asked you about the dwelling of Johan Tarculovski in 2001, where he lived with his wife, did you try to establish contact with Valentina Radulevic, the then-wife of Johan Tarculovski, so that she gives you the data about their residence address and whether they lived together with someone else?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Kenan Salievski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him, yes. If you mean Kenan Salievski from Ljuboten, yes. The answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He is the village leader of Ljuboten; in 2001 he was. Or one of the village leaders, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have access to the statement of Kenan Salievski, dated 6th and 7th of November, 2004?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And he stated to your colleague, the investigator, that Rafet Bajrami and Shefajet Bajrami, brothers of the victims Xhelal and Sulejman Bajrami, were NLA members. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could put the -- give me the corresponding paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 1D85, page 9, paragraph 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Asked who among the Ljuboten villagers were NLA members, Kenan Salievski states Suad Saliu, Riza Jonuzi and he then enumerates other persons among whom are Shefajet Bajrami as well and Rafet Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also you had an interview with Baki Alimi, another village leader of Ljuboten in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And he also told you that the brother of Sulejman Bajrami was an NLA member. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recollect it precisely, but I believe so, yes. Please show me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 1D876, paragraph 1, page 5. Could we please zoom in on the name Sulejman Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And Baki Halimi, one of the village leaders of Ljuboten in 2001, when speaking about Sulejman Bajrami, he says that his brother was an NLA member. Can you agree with me on that now?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read here that under the name Sulejman Bajrami it says not a member of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is written then on the bottom, his brother was in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood the question to say that you were referring to Sulejman Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise. Maybe I misspoke when asking you the question, but my question was referring to his brother.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As regards his brother, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Open session].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have information as to Shefajet Bajrami being within the group that planted the mine on the 10th of August, 2001, when Macedonian soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that, no. I couldn't tell you. It's a very wide and open question. I cannot really have a complete overview of the entire material.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then I would ask you, did you interview Shefajet Bajrami so that you could get more information about his membership in the NLA and his presence at Ljuboten on the 8th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We could not localise Shefajet, couldn't find him. If I remember correctly, we would need to go back to the statement with Baki Alimi, and also, as I mentioned, it was in conjunction with the name of the father, Aziz Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you requested from the Macedonian government to provide witnesses that were not accessible to you through a request for assistance?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened quite frequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you request from the Macedonian government to provide Shefajet Bajrami for you?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that when you were in the Ministry of Interior Affairs, you photocopied Johan Tarculovski's file. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in regards with the following question, since we had problems with the e-court, I have one document from the file of Johan Tarculovski. The document is in hard copy, if I could ask that this document is distributed to the Chamber and all parties. This is an unofficial translation. This is document 65 ter 01075, page N006-6225. Since the document was only in the Macedonian language, we made an unofficial translation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this questionnaire that was photocopied to you? This is from Johan Tarculovski's file.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see the translation here, though, but it sounds plausible, and I think I can remember. And of course you must be showing me the correct document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The court manager opened the English -- the Macedonian version of this document on your monitor. Can you see the middle of the page where there is a question about knowledge of a foreign language and it's written "English." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And below, it is said he speaks English and he uses German.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I could -- I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any indication of the date of its creation, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On the next page, it is said that this is a document from 1998. On the photocopy it is not very legible, but in my opinion, it was a document of -- made in December 1998. This is on the second page, and this also will be translated and will be distributed to everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document is already Exhibit P533, I'm told, Mr. Apostolski, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But, Your Honours, it has not been completely translated, so we did not know if it was accepted as an exhibit as a whole or just the pages that were translated and the pages that my learned colleague from the Prosecution used to examine the witness. This was, as far as I remember, the decision for employment of Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The entire document was exhibited. It is helpfully suggested we might simply include this draft translation in that exhibit. Would that be convenient, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, you had access to the police archives and evidence of persons that are perpetrators of crime. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You had access to the prosecution's archives. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it quite like that. We didn't have access to the archives. We asked for the release of the files of the prosecution and the investigation judges, and this request was granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in -- that in any evidence about crime perpetrators, the name of Johan Tarculovski was registered as a perpetrator of a crime and that there were no criminal reports against him and there were no judgments made by Macedonian courts that were against him?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that to be correct. But I would need to read up on that. Because this request, of course, was not only pertaining to the files of the -- of a tribunal but also of the records of the police. But I believe you are right. As far as I can remember, no, he doesn't have any criminal record.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Clearly this is a convenient moment, then, for the first break. We resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the transcript I wish to inform the Court that with regards to Exhibit 2D41, there will be an official translation. The CLSS will send it to the e-court under 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the court officer will attach it to the original document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly ask the Defence counsel to repeat the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 2D419.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to clarify one point that arose from today, you were asked if the number 070279417 was used or you received information that number was "used by Gjorgi Todorovski." Can I ask you, was the information that you received from the Macedonian authorities, was that telephone number, was it used by Gjorgi Todorovski or was the information relating to who the number was subscribed to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is true, Ms. Issa. I can give you the required information. The information pertained to subscriber. I was not informed that he used the phone number. And, Your Honour, Ms. Issa, if I like I would like to briefly correct something to what was just said before the break if you allow. Thank you. During the break I very quickly read up on something regarding to a question asked by Mr. Apostolski, which concerned a criminal record and pertaining to RFA 77 of 13 September 2004. The OTP was informed that Mr. Johan Tarculovski did have a file in SVR Skopje in which a violation of Article 12 was -- alleged there was a physical attack. The date of the offence being committed was 25 April 1992. Whether this constitutes a prior conviction in the criminal sense or not, I do not know. I simply wanted to add this for completeness sake. I did not have time to check exactly on one of the other questions you asked me because a colleague did this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to address the Court once again and indicate that my question was related to criminal record, not misdemeanour record, so I wish to have this clear. My question was pertaining to criminal record while the witness is now testifying to -- with regards to a misdemeanour record and there is a difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuehnel, at transcript page 814 -- 8014 you were asked about the president having used Mr. Keskovski's phone during the weekend of 10 to 12 August 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can go to the statement of Mr. Keskovski at 1D526, please, and so save time I can just indicate that referring you to paragraph 32 of the statement. It says that: "Johan Tarculovski called me," and this is Mr. Keskovski's speaking on that day, which is the 10th of August, 2001, "sometime in the afternoon and asked for at least two days off, since he had a relative who died in the incident and he would like to join funeral. According to the law, he was entitled to have at least two days off. I gave him at least two days off. I do not know what relation Johan Tarculovski was with the death of the soldiers. I even do not know the names of the victims of Ljubotenski Bacila." And then the next paragraph says: "I informed the president, according to a standard procedure, that some of the killed soldiers were relatives of Johan Tarculovski and that he had asked for at least two days off." Then in paragraph 34 of that statement: "In the afternoon on the 10th of August, the president approved the request and asked me to call Johan Tarculovski. As I called Johan Tarculovski, the president wanted to speak to him so that I gave him my mobile phone. I was present during the conversation and I heard the president asking Johan Tarculovski to call the next day and inform the president about the situation in the village. The president was concerned that if there was unrest at the village, it could postpone the signing of the Ohrid Agreement which was scheduled for Monday, 13th of August 2001." Now, Mr. Kuehnel, does it say anything in there that the president is to call Mr. Tarculovski about the operation?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I could then just take you to paragraph 39 of the statement on the next page. "After the above-mentioned conversation, Johan Tarculovski called on my mobile phone and he said that in Ljuboten there is an action being prepared." "And then it continues and he says: "I asked him who was preparing the action and he replied that it was the police and the army units." And then it continues and it says: "I asked him what the problem was and he said the problem was a certain army major - I do not know his name - who did not want to undertake any activities because he did not receive any orders from his superior officers." And then, if if we go to paragraph 40 he says that: "I told Tarculovski to put the major on the phone. I did not ask the major his name; only his rank and superior officer." And then it says: "The person told me that he was in rank of major and his superior was General Sokol Mitrevski. I still held on the phone and I explained to the president what the situation was. The president asked me to give him the phone because he wanted to speak to the major." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: "Before handing the phone to the president, I asked the major if he would obey an order coming directly from the supreme commander, which means the president." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, yesterday at transcript page 8075 you were asked whether -- did you see -- whether you saw other information where the president sought to reach Mr. Tarculovski on the phone and you referred to evidence in Mr. Keskovski's statement, Despodov, Kostadinov and Kopacev reports. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can go to paragraph 41 of the statement, refers to: "The president asked what his rank and superior's name, and that's continuing on from the previous paragraph. I did not hear the replies from the major to the president, but I heard as the president told the major to make sure the operation goes according to the plans and he would call his superior Sokol Mitrovski." Is this the conversation that you were referring to, where you -- yesterday -- where the president spoke to Major Despodov and said that Despodov will be contacted by General Mitrevski, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is as you say. It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In the cross-examination at transcript page 8017, you were also shown part of paragraph 42 in this statement and you were shown the part in the middle of the paragraph where it says: "When I spoke with Johan Tarculovski I used my mobile phone." And then there were two numbers that are you given and then it says: "I do not know the number of the president -- the mobile phone because we were changing it frequently. For instance, I took the phone from a driver and I gave it to the president and vice versa." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you look at the top of that paragraph at paragraph 42?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hm-mmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it says: "During course of the conversation between me and Johan Tarculovski he never mentioned that he is involved in the operation, anyway, and the first time," and then it continues. And that refers to that one conversation, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And apart from the conversation where the president had expressed concern for a possible unrest might postpone the Ohrid Agreement, there's nothing in this statement which says that the president spoke directly to Johan Tarculovski regarding the operation, is there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I did not see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we could then please go to P00464. Now this is from the war -- the book titled: The War in Macedonia in 2001. If we can please turn to ERN page number N006-3017. If we can actually -- if we can go to the 8th page after that, please. If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, I think -- thank you, Madam Registrar, I do see the correct page on the screen now. Apologies for the delay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see, Mr. Kuehnel, underneath the heading, Orders, the use of the police during martial law to support the army, about the third paragraph underneath that that begins with: "Since martial law was not declared. The second sentence says -- begins with: "One can only imagine what the situation is like when two ministers from the same government (the Ministry of Interior, and Ministry of Defence) have two armed components at their disposal,, one of which is commanded by the prime minister through the minister of the interior, while the other is under the command of the president of the Republic through the Defence minister." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if you look at the second paragraph below that, which begins with, As a result, it says: "As a result, it could be said that the two armed structures, the police and the army, were each fighting on their own front. This type of deployment of the police as the prime minister's armed force caused a rift in the management and command of the joint security forces of the Republic of Macedonia." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, in Mr. Keskovski's statement which we looked at, that paragraph 9, the head of the prime minister's security was Vlatko Stefanovski, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to P00369 at page 4. And at the moment we are looking at the outgoing calls for the number believed to be Johan Tarculovski's number 70279417. And if I can draw your attention to about the 8th line down, do you see that, it says that Johan Tarculovski's number called on the 10th of August, 2001, Vlatko Stefanovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please go to page 56 where the incoming calls -- the log-book for the incoming calls begins. Yes, that's the correct page. Now, if you see, Mr. Kuehnel, at about the sixth column down, there are two calls to the number 279417, and that -- and on the 10th of August, 2001, from the security of the prime minister. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to the next page. And, again, if you look at the -- about the -- sorry. About the sixth column down, once again, on the 11th of August 2001, the security of the prime minister called Johan Tarculovski's number. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can we please turn to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you look at about the 13th column down from the top, once again, the security of the prime minister called Johan Tarculovski on 13 August 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if I can please ask Madam Registrar to go back to page 56.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you look at about the middle of the page, there's a name of Goran Stojkov who called Johan Tarculovski's number on the 10th of August 2001 twice, at 12.37 and at 10.54, respectively. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who is Goran Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Stojkov, as far as I'm aware, is a police general or he was in 2001. At that time one can say that he had a dual function. In the security service he worked for the prime minister and according to his own statements he also was involved in setting up the unit later, better known as the Lions formation, and even later than that he became the leader of that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interfering with my learned friend's examination, but she states, as if it were a fact several times. On page 35, lines 2 and 3 she states that Goran Stojkov has called Johan Tarculovski, has called Johan Tarculovski's number twice. From the evidence of this witness, he stated that there has been a connection between two telephone numbers. He never indicated that it was a fact, a certain fact that it was Johan Tarculovski's phone number or Goran Stojkov's phone number. So I would like to ask my colleague to be more careful in framing the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. I don't think I need to underline what's been said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I take the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have been actually noting in my notes the telephone number each time you said Johan Tarculovski's phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I should have said what is believed to be Johan Tarculovski's phone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not even that. It's merely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What you believe to be, yes. No. You're quite correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please call up what is marked for identification as P00379, and while that's being called up, Mr. Kuehnel, you recall that you were asked at some point, at transcript page 8037 whether you were aware of any recorded calls from Mr. Boskoski to Mr. Tarculovski during the period of 10 to 12 August, 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether there were any calls between Mr. Boskoski and (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I already explained, I cannot tell you with the utmost certainty because these are all connection data. What I do know is that (redacted), when he was questioned, stated he been in telephone contact with Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to the Macedonian -- in the Macedonian version, page 8 and in the English version N000-8927. And if I can ask Madam Registrar to please turn to the following page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that my colleague is about to enter into an area of questioning which we have not touched upon for obvious reasons, and I believe she's about to ask questions about the suggestion made by one particular witness about the allegation which he made about phone contacts between himself and Mr. Boskoski. I believe that this witness, Mr. Kuehnel, has given the evidence which he was capable of giving on that particular issue and which he knew from having interviewed the person in question. We believe, however, that the witness in question is still to appear. The allegations --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- will be tested with him, Your Honour, and furthermore, we believe that this document in particular is the subject of a pending motion before Your Honour on its admissibility. We therefore believe that the witness hereby present is not an appropriate witness to whom this document should be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I will simply refer to a very brief portion of this interview. After the reference to "on the 10th on the road," which refers to August 10th, if you look at about the middle of the page, I don't know if you see that on your screen. Perhaps we can scroll down very -- just towards the bottom of the screen. It says: "The next day the soldiers were buried at the time I was called personally on the phone by -- Minister Ljube Boskoski phoned and told me that a person by name Johan will come to me, who is in his personal security and that if he requests any services, I have orders from him to carry them out." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware of this information, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I already read about this. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please briefly go back to P00369.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we proceed and perhaps to clarify the matter, since the Prosecution was permitted to pursue this line of questioning, if my colleague could ask the witness whether the allegation that was made by the witness, the person who was talked to, whether this allegation was in any way supported by the telephone records which the witness, Mr. Kuehnel, reviewed in his capacity as an investigator, that may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I -- I can ask the witness questions to see if he can answer the question, Your Honour. I don't know at this point. But I can certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you -- Mr. Kuehnel, did you actually check the telephone records to determine whether or not you could see this telephone call that -- that we referred to moments ago?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did do that. But I really would need to read up on it carefully again. But what I can say is that I did not find any record with the name of Ljube Boskoski in this telephone register. The problem is that we received about six to eight telephone numbers with the comment that they were being used by Mr. Ljube Boskoski, but it was also quite possible that the telephone numbers were being used by others. But I'm quite careful in saying this, because the evidence pertaining to the person is missing, that somebody made a statement to the effect that he heard the voice of Mr. Boskoski with this particular number for this moment in time. But I really would need to read up on that. We've checked it, but I cannot give you any definitive answer at this moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to page 12 of P00369, the outgoing calls.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now you see at the very top of that page, Mr. Kuehnel, right below the telephone calls to Mr. Ljube Krstevski we see a call from that number, 279417, to the UBK. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's on the 13th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd just like to move to another area. Now, you were asked some questions a couple of days ago regarding the possibility that a criminal report may have been conveyed orally to an investigating judge, and that's at transcript pages 8054 to 8056. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you were, I believe, shown a reference --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see Mr. Mettraux is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleague, Your Honour. It's simply for the clarity of the record. I think we said criminal report to the Prosecutor and information to the investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You were also shown a reference to a phone call from P00535, which is, you may recall, the outgoing calls log-book for Ljube Krstevski's telephone number, indicating that Mr. Krstevski called an investigative judge and it was suggested to you that a criminal report could have been made orally. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember that, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, as an experienced investigator, would you except that a criminal report to the public prosecutor or information to the investigative judge of such serious crimes as those alleged to have been carried out by the police or members of the Ministry of Interior in Ljuboten would have been made in writing?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, yes. I don't think that a telephone call would be sufficient, and I think I have already stated that. I just can't imagine that. I cannot imagine that for the situation of the police in Macedonia for that, they certainly would be too professional to handle this just via a simple telephone call.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if the public prosecutor had received such reports, whether they were in writing or orally, would you expect to find such documentation within the court files?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least I would make a note in the files about this -- I would assume that there would be a note in the files about this conversation and then I would assume that further measures would be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And were there any such documentation that you found either within the Ministry of Interior or the court files in connection to police criminal conduct in Ljuboten in 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't find it in any case, and I looked at both documentations of the investigative judge files and prosecutor's files and I didn't find anything. The only thing which in place and time would coincide would be the information on the 14th of August as regards the so-called crime scene inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, but we feel we have to intervene in relation to this line of questioning. We would simply like to indicate that there is a document in evidence already which is an Official Note prepared by the then investigative judge Mr. Ognen Stavrev that specifically records this fact and this document has been now admitted in evidence. We believe that to the extent that the Prosecutor is trying to suggest, if indeed that is what is being done, we believe the line of questioning, in our submission, Your Honour, could be somewhat improper since the document in question in fact records that very event happening in the case of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'd have to refer to the document that Mr. Mettraux is referring to. But I don't believe it records criminal conduct or allegations of criminal conduct by the police in Ljuboten in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, what the document suggests is the fact that the investigative judge Mr. Stavrev was in fact informed orally by the duty centre of the MOI about the events of Ljuboten by -- in other words, by the police or the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you feel the need to look to the document or are you content to carry on, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm content to carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuehnel, did you find any information relating to the criminal conduct of the police in Ljuboten in 2001 which indicated that the -- the matter was being investigated?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in a single case I found anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions in relation to the law on amnesty, and in your examination-in-chief at pages 7893 to 7894 you said that you were aware of a response from the Ministry of Interior to a request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor, indicating that no non-Albanian individual was subject to a criminal investigation, indictment or any other procedure in connection to the events in Ljuboten during the time-period of 10 to 12 August 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to P000048.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have got a question, Ms. Issa. I don't know whether it is possible or necessary. You asked me about this telephone number of UBK a few sentences before. I don't know whether you require any further explanation about that or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think I've --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] You've covered it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, it's covered. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, we see here as one example of a decision to exempt an arrested member of the so-called NLA from criminal prosecution. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it is signed by the then president Boris Trajkovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, would you expect to have found similar written documentation granting amnesty to police perpetrators had they been charged with crimes or investigated for crimes in connection with the Ljuboten events and subsequently granted amnesty?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would expect that. And I think I've already stated that during my previous interview, that for specific case and for a specific accused I would expect such a document as far as amnesty is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the first one on my feet, Your Honours. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've been awarded the prize, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe the witness is misled with this, so at least once I was the first one on my feet and I was faster than my colleague Mettraux. I think that the witness has been misled. This is a decision on pardoning and I do not think this is a decision based on the Law on Amnesty. Pardon and amnesty are two different legal notions and the Law on Amnesty was passed in 2001 [as interpreted], so on the basis of Law on Amnesty, you could not show this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My colleague was not only faster; he was also better than me, Your Honour. The same point was to be made by the defence of Mr. Boskoski. I believe, however, that the transcript should read that the Law of amnesty was passed in 2002, not in 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Issa, we seem to have some suggested confusion between an amnesty and a pardon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps if I can ask a few more questions it can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't have to rely on that document necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, irrespective of the document that we just saw if someone were to be granted amnesty from such serious allegatons or crimes that were committed as alleged in this case in Ljuboten in 2001, would you expect to have found some written documentation relating to the granting of such amnesty?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would indeed expect that. At least a document which would explain the allegation and then would also give the reasons as to why this pardon or this amnesty should have been granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, there are legal distinctions between an amnesty, usually an amnesty against prosecution, and a pardon for any offences that may have been committed. I think your questioning may continue to blur that distinction and the evidence of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will leave that at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is why I was on my feet, Your Honours. The pardon is an individual act while the amnesty is prescribed by the law and it is directed generally to anyone involved, while the pardon is an individual act by which the president grants pardon to a given individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think we'll pause to go right through the full scope of both, but I think it's enough to say that there is some confusion in the questioning at the present time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Would Your Honour like me to carry on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just moving on to another topic. Mr. Kuehnel, you were asked at some stage at transcript page 8046 whether you were aware that a particular individual heard a conversation on the radio which suggested that Mr. Qaili had been handling a hand-grenade and you said that it may have been contained in some investigator note from Zoran Cvetanovski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that investigator note actually indicates that a -- that he-- Mr. Qaili was alleged to have been found in possession of the hand-grenade. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to P0023.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now that's an Official Note submitted by Sasa Simonovic on 12 August 2001. And it lists the ammunition and weapons that were seized from the villagers or the Ljuboten detainees on that date. Do you see any reference to a grenade listed as part of the cache of weapons. And for the record it includes the number -- the detainees include Atulla Qaili. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, and I can see any indication about a confiscated grenade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to P0054. Actually, the ERN number that I have is ERN N000-7278.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if you can please look at that document, Mr. Kuehnel. It's dated 13 August 2001. It's submitted by Blagoja Toskovski, an official -- and the subject heading is official conversation carried out with the persons taken over from the village of Ljuboten and it lists the following persons, one of them being Atulla Qaili. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know this document, yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the last paragraph in that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please scroll down to the end of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it says, "Regarding the weapon and ammunition found on them during their arrest, the same men stated that they have not used it. At the place the persons were found and arrested, the following weapons and ammunition were found." And it lists an automatic rifle of Chinese production. Actually lists two automatic rifles of Chinese production. Do you see any reference to a hand-grenade or a grenade in that document, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see that. This document has got a second page, and even on the following page there's -- you can't see any indications to that. It's -- it doesn't say anywhere in any of the documents that a grenade has been confisicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, this was Exhibit P24.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, at transcript pages 8062 to 8063, you were asked about the investigation that the Office of the Prosecutor commenced regarding the matter that is before the Chamber. And you were specifically asked about colliding investigations. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to P0073.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision by then minister Ljube Boskoski establishing the commission on -- dated 13 August 2001. And it refers to the task to review circumstances and analyse activities undertaken by the security forces of the Ministry of Interior to repel armed attacks of the terrorist groups on 12 August 2001 in Ljuboten. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to P00054.4. Do you see the date of that document is 14 August 2001, and it's from the deputy public prosecutor. If we go down to the second page, we can see that. And it's titled as a request for enforcement of investigation with the proposal to impose detention and it lists the names of the individuals that are -- that were alleged to have committed crimes or to -- in relation to the proposal to impose detention. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you agree, Mr. Kuehnel, that based on these two documents, there was an investigation commenced by the Ministry of Interior and a simultaneous and parallel investigation commenced by the basic public prosecutor. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to intervene again, but we submit again that this line of questioning is in fact improper. When we asked the particular question which counsel suggests entitles the Prosecutor to ask question in re-examination, my question was as follows: "Mr. Kuehnel, perhaps you have answered it already, but are you aware that the reason or one of the reason invoked by the Office of the Prosecutor in September of 2002 for the deferral of five cases, including the case of Ljuboten, to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal, was the risk of colliding investigations between your investigation and the investigation conducted at the local level? Are you aware of that fact?" And the answer of Mr. Kuehnel was: "I cannot give you any reply to that, really. It is a possible reason but I really haven't got a complete overview over that time-period and about all the decisions that were taken and by whom. Hence, if I confirm or disagree, I could only give you a very incomplete account." Your Honour, as a result of that - and this was page 8062 and 8063 - the Defence moved on to a different subject. We only gave the indication about a particular document. However, we had a series of documents, letters from the Prosecution, letters to the Prosecution, decisions, Prosecution requests, Trial Chamber decisions in relation to this matter. The Prosecutor, in various letters sent in particular in the year 2002 acknowledged and the Chief Prosecutor of this Tribunal also acknowledged the fact of an ongoing investigation in the matter of Ljuboten. They are plenty of documents which suggest that fact. We submit, Your Honour, and with no criticism of our colleague, I insist that the line of questioning is improper to the extent that it would suggest that there was no investigation ongoing at the time, whereas the Office of the Prosecutor itself has acknowledged that fact on many repeated occasion, in particular in the year of 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was merely asking that question picking up from the cross-examination regarding the suggestion that was put to Mr. Kuehnel about the, quote/unquote, colliding investigations. I wasn't planning on taking it any further than the -- than what I have already done. But in my respectful submission, it was proper re-examination in light of the suggestions that were put by Mr. Mettraux despite the fact that he did not carry on with further questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point of your re-examination being to -- to identify the investigation that was instituted at the request of the deputy public prosecutor on the 14th of August? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the point, Your Honour, was to demonstrate that it's quite possible for two parallel investigations to -- to take place without interfering with -- with one another, which is what I took the suggestion to be from Mr. Mettraux's suggestion or questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think counsel are a very long way apart in what each perceives to be the issue and how they are approaching it. You say you intended to go no further than you have. We will leave it there and carry on with whatever else. Now, is it a convenient time now or is there something you wish to finish at this moment?
