utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It would be a convenient time at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now and we'll resume at five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I believe yesterday you were asked questions regarding the existence of a commission for the centralised police service in 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to Prosecution Exhibit P526 and if it could please not be broadcast. I just note for the record it's under seal. If we can please turn to page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see at the very top of the document, right below the minutes, it says the MVR dismissal commission formed with the minister's decision number, and then it lists a number of names of the composition of the commission. Now, you have had an opportunity to review this file, Mr. Kuehnel, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you say that that's an example of a commission within the centralised police service based on your review of the material and your understanding?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a good example. It's an analog way which we handled the centralised police units. In the year 2001, the -- that's how we dealt with it. If the name -- even if the name was not in existence then, but that is the centralised police unit of the Ministry of the Interior, as is known.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can then -- you were also actually shown a passage in the same exhibit. I think Mr. Mettraux is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, but simply for the record, our understanding is that this is the permanent disciplinary commission, not the, quote/unquote, special commission that Mr. Kuehnel indicated is a different commission. This is our understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Proceed with your questioning, please, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You were also shown yesterday a passage in the same exhibit that essentially shows - and if I can refer you back to page 2 of that exhibit - that shows the minister, then minister Ljube Boskoski exercising his power to transfer his power to Risto Galevski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can take you to page 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask Madam Registrar to go to page 8, please. And -- actually, we're at page 7 right now and just by way of introduction to page 8, that refers to the hearing whereby (redacted) is testifying or providing evidence. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, and that's at page 6. If we can then please go to page 8. If we can just go two pages down, please. And if I can ask Madam Registrar to focus on the bottom of that page. Now, if I can just draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the last couple of passages in the very bottom of that page, where it says: "A short time afterwards the minister also rang me and asked how far we had got. I replied that the unit and I were on the way back to Skopje. The minister started threatening me, saying that we were deserters, that we would have -- and that he would have us all thrown in the lockup and demanding that we immediately make a list of all the members who did not want to take part in the operation. Mr. Kuehnel, would you say that the minister in that instance exercised his power to intervene despite having transferred power to Risto Galevski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although, Ms. Issa, there is a very good example for a leadership personage to take direct -- have direct influence exerted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you can please just clarify your last sentence, what you mean by that. When you said although. Is there something that you wish to add?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That could have been a translation. What I actually meant was although in a sense of indeed I agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if we can then please go to page 3 of that same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, it's actually the second page after the -- within the decision, within the part of the document titled Decision. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now I believe yesterday you were shown this part of the decision, signed by Mr. Boskoski, and it was drawn to your attention that an officer may appeal against this decision. We see that at the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you also see the line immediately after that that says: "An appeal against this decision does not defer the implementation of the decision?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if we can please go to Exhibit 1D1141.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. I believe it is Rule 65 ter, Your Honour, 1D1141.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, it is also Exhibit 1D275, now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now at the very top that refers to Article 143, item 5 of the collective agreement of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Do you see that, among other things?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you recall, that referred, that Article referred to the proposal for initiation of the disciplinary procedure that can be submitted by persons authorised by the minister. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, would you say that that's an example of the minister's fundamental authority to -- over the entire disciplinary process and his power to decentralise disciplinary procedures?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. I see that he has a general overview and obviously also authority over the whole process, including the authority to delegate. He has to be in this function in order to exercise these competences, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could we please go to P000382. That's a collective agreement that we looked at yesterday. If you can please go to page N002-6377, Madam Registrar. I think it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just drawing your attention to Article 149 of the collective agreement it says that "If the minister does not agree with the proposal, he can return the case for additional review," and then at the end it continues, "or the minister might bring a different decision or a decision according to Article 139, paragraph 1, of this agreement." Without going over back over the disciplinary files that we looked at during the course of the examination-in-chief, do you recall seeing examples, Mr. Kuehnel, where the minister changed the proposal made by the commission, either by changing the mode of punishment or reducing the pecuniary punishment proposed by a commission?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, while I studied these files, I noticed several times that obviously, the practical interpretation of this article has in several cases meant the commission's proposal was deviated from and that the minister apparently exercised his right to influence the duration of whatever punishment had been decided or to reduce the punishment. That struck me. And every time at the end of every proceeding, the minister's signature had been put at the last document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreter please request that Ms. Issa perhaps switches off her microphone when the witness is speaking, so otherwise, we hear the rustling of the notes. I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will take care to do that. If we can then please go to what was 65 ter 1D1142, and I'm sorry, Madam Registrar, I didn't note down the exhibit number that was given out today.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We believe it to be Exhibit 1D276, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just want to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the very top before it says decision, where it refers to Article 55, item 1 of the Law on Organisation and Work of the Bodies of the State Authority. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It also refers to Article 143 of the collective agreement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to P00092. If we can first go to Article 55, please. I believe it's on page 15 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just want to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to item 1 of Article 55, which says that the minister submits rule, orders, guidelines, plans, et cetera, when he is authorised to do so by law. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can then draw your attention to Article 57, right below that, if I can ask Madam Registrar to scroll down. It also says: "The minister submits decisions on administrative proceedings and departmental questions as well as on other cases anticipated by law or other regulations." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you were asked some questions I believe it was yesterday, you were asked whether Ms. Naumova that you spoke to when you were obtaining the documents from the permanent disciplinary commission said that the disciplinary proceedings would be initiated against identified individuals or known perpetrators. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, would it be easier to initiate a disciplinary proceeding against a known perpetrator if steps had been taken to identify the perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we simply wanted to give a chance perhaps to the witness if he wish to hear his answer, but we really believe that this is in the realm of absolute hypotheticals. And the other matter which we would to bring to the attention, as indicated by Mr. Kuehnel in response to my question, I believe, is he was in fact told by Ms. Naumova what we understand to be the correct position in the law in Macedonia is that the procedure can only be triggered against known individuals. The question, in our respectful submissions, is not only contrary to what Ms. Naumova told Mr. Kuehnel but also contrary to what the law says. But if Your Honour wish to hear the answer of Mr. Kuehnel, obviously we'll say no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I believe that I've indicated that the question -- that Ms. Naumova had said that disciplinary procedures would be initiated against identified individuals. That's at about -- that's at page 61 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yeah. There's no question about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yeah. And then this is simply a follow-up question to clarify and to follow up on that question that I believe Mr. Mettraux has put to the witness in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The issue is a proposal for dismissal, is it not? That's what the procedure is?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the issue is whether or not one can initiate a disciplinary proceedings against a perpetrator that has been identified or known. And so the question is, how can that be done unless steps would -- could be taken or were taken to identify those individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm missing something here. You are trying to put the proposition that there has to be somebody identified in the proposal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm trying to put the proposition that there must be somebody identified in order to initiate proceedings against an individual person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, isn't that what Mr. Kuehnel has said is his understanding?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's correct. And as a follow-up to that, I simply asked whether it would have been easier to initiate proceedings against an identified person or a known person if steps had been taken to identify that person in the first place. Perhaps it might be a question of semantics, Your Honour, but I need not go any further if Your Honour doesn't wish me to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think we're going to be helped.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You were also asked, Mr. Kuehnel, about a conversation with Ms. Naumova regarding whether disciplinary proceedings apply to reservists, and what my question is to you, is there anything precluding the minister of the interior or his subordinates from referring criminal conduct to the appropriate authorities, such as the prosecutor or investigative judge that relate to reservists?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see anything which would exclude any such proceedings. On the contrary, the way I would interpret this, in general, on the basis of the disciplinary proceedings knowledge I have derived from the police, that would actually constitute an important element of what call a self-purification process within the police authorities. Namely, if there are any incidents which prove to be relevant and might lead to criminal charges, then these will not be prevented. That can also be done in parallel to disciplinary proceedings instigated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And to save time, Mr. Kuehnel, in your examination-in-chief do you recall seeing a file of one Milan Mitrevski that you found within the permanent disciplinary commission whereby a charges -- criminal charges were in fact referred to the appropriate authorities against a reservist?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, that's Exhibit P528. You were also asked questions about 65 ter 1D937, which was an investigator note regarding a -- an individual called Bogeski.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the spelling of the name is quite correct. I would need to read up on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the name that I believe that you were asked about was Stojance Bogeski.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you were asked about whether he -- Stojance Bogeski stated that he was serving his duty at a combined military and police check-point. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you recall, Mr. Kuehnel, that according to the investigator's comments who met with Mr. Bogeski that he found him to be an individual who was looking for employment and that he was attempting to help the ICTY in view of obtaining financial gain?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Has there been any evidence in the course of your investigation, Mr. Kuehnel, that shows there were mixed check-points during the relevant period of time of military and police?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I have already declared, it's just the opinion of one person and didn't correspond to what I could see, and also relating to the specific check-point, this is -- which is mentioned in this investigator's note.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You were also asked whether some of the persons that were interviewed in relation to whether or not they received weapons on the 25th or 26th of July from PSOLO that were actually -- who were named on the list on Exhibit P00436 had indicated to you or members of the investigating team that they had not received weapons from PSOLO. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just would like to clarify, Mr. Kuehnel, did any of the persons that were interviewed on that list indicate or admit that they in fact had received weapons from PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The majority of the persons that we questioned and interrogated have admitted to that. And as I have already stated, we interviewed about 15 to 19 persons. I can't recollect precisely. At any rate, the majority openly admitted to that, especially when we submitted the lists with -- bearing their signatures, and this was a procedure which was credible, because we also questioned the administrator of this unit and he stated so, and we then submitted the list with the signatures of these persons. And in these particular cases where it was stated they had arms, equipment and uniforms and they -- they admitted to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to clarify, when you say, "We also questioned the administrator of this unit and he stated so," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. You also indicated -- or you were asked questions regarding your attendance at the Dal Met Fu Hotel and at pages 8126 to 8127, you were asked questions or you referred to noticing that one book, as you say, appeared to be newer than the other one, and this is in reference to the hotel foreign guest book registry. Can you please explain which book appeared to be newer to you, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was under the impression that the first book, the book dated 2001, looked considerably more recent. As regards the wear and tear of the book, the way it looked, that was my impression so it looked newer to me compared to the second book, which was used after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that book was -- the second book that you refer to is from the period of March 2002 to March 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I understand you took some photographs regarding the condition of the books when you attended at this hotel, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did so, and I tried to take a photograph of the outward appearance of the books, then the inside pages at the beginning and at the end, as I was not allowed to take photos of the actual content of the books. And the photos that I did take, the partial photos, I tried to make photographs, to take photographs of the seals and the binding of the book, so everything that was joined to the seal in the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please go to 65 ter 1077. And if I can ask Madam Registrar to go to ERN number N003-8004. Thank you. Is this one of the photographs that you took, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to -- sorry, I should ask which -- do you recognise which book that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe we could zoom in a little bit more, please. Yes, that is book number 1, The first book, dated 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to N003-8032.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And which book does that depict?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's obviously book number 2, which was -- which followed the first in sequence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please go to N003-8065. Can you indicate briefly what that depicts?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you can see both books put on top of each other, and lying on the length side. You can see the paper and the different colouring of the paper and also different condition of the pages, which are slightly waved and obviously the spaces compared -- between the top book and the lower book. You can also see that -- what you can see on the right-hand side from my perspective, you can see the folded corners and also the traces that show wear and tear. The lower book dates back to the year 2001, and the upper book is book number 2, which followed after.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, finally, if we can go to N003-8219, please. And if you can just very briefly, Mr. Kuehnel, indicate what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture again shows both books. In the lower half you can see the book dated back to 2001 and then the book after that, on top, and it shows you the condition of both books on the first page, when you open up the books. On the right-hand side, at the top and at the bottom, you can see two holes, and they then continue right through the book right to the back page, and then you can you see a string going through these two holes. And there is also a seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would just like to tender this at this stage, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean the one, two, three, four photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. I think they're listed under 65 ter exhibit 1077 and I was seeking to tender them as one exhibit, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have no objection to the pictures being tendered, but perhaps a matter which could be of assistance to the Chamber when assessing this matter would to be ask Mr. Kuehnel if he knows the period of time during which both books were in use at the hotel in question, since this may or may not be relevant to the Chamber's assessment of the conditions of the books. We believe it may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm -- it is drawn to my attention, Ms. Issa that the e-court document is in fact 13 photographs. You want just these four; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That may take a little longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no difficulty having all of the photographs contained in that e-court document admitted. I simply didn't want to waste the Court's time by showing them all to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's fine. It's just that it will produce a technical problem, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The four photographs will be received as one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P542, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A matter was raised by Mr. Mettraux. Do you want to pursue that in way?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe Mr. Mettraux has already asked the witness questions of this nature during the course of his cross-examination, if I recollect correctly, and I don't intend on pursuing it, subject to Your Honours, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for the interruption. Since I did not deal with this book, I would like the witness to tell me whether both were registered by the Ministry of Interior affairs and I would like to highlight that one of the photographs I think where the older book is -- or let me correct, one book was put on the top of the other, and it is normal that the book on the top is actually putting some pressure on the book that is below, and this does not give truthful image of the photograph. I want to ask whether the witness has photographed the books the other way around, the book that was under the first one to be put on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber makes no specific direction in respect of those matters, Ms. Issa. It would be a matter for you, whether you wish to pursue any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we may please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, you were asked questions regarding Mr. Hutsch yesterday and whether you were able to interview Jonce Popovski, one of the names given to you by Mr. Hutsch, and another name, and this is at transcript page 8130 and you said he could not be located by the ministry when you attempted to find these two individuals. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Didn't Mr. Hutsch also mention a Goran Stojkov in connection to the Ljuboten events on 12 August 2001 in his statement as well?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And was he located by the ministry and ultimately interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor or spoken to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That was very easy. He was in prison at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, you will be please to know that that concludes the questions for you in this trial. The Chamber would thank you for your assistance and you're of course now free to go about your normal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We need now to adjourn now, given the hour, so perhaps we could ask you just to remain seated a moment while we do. We must adjourn at the moment with it indefinite and unknown when exactly we can come together to hear the remaining witness or some other steps taken. We simply are delayed at the moment because the witness is not presently available in The Hague. The Chamber's legal officer will be in touch with the parties, advising when the Chamber would propose to reassemble to continue the hearing, and we are actively seeking advise as to when the witness might be available to give his evidence. Now, that is likely to extend during next week, as far as can be presently assessed. It is both frustrating for the timely completion of the trial and frustrating in that we cannot make definite decisions or plans at the present time. If as the week -- next week, that is, progresses and there is no certainty, could I indicate that the Chamber would certainly be prepared to receive motions from any party about the future course, whatever they may wish, but in the absence of that, a time will come when, because of the time and because of what we have learnt, the Chamber will call the parties together. But I cannot at this moment, I regret to say, tell you exactly when that will be -- there will be a more than a day's notice if anybody needs to travel out of The Hague. On that unsatisfactory basis, I'm afraid we must now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened sine die.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
